edges.reason: transfer() forwards execution into transferFrom(msg.sender, _to, _value).
msg.sender is passed as the _from argument into transferFrom even though it is attacker controlled.
ensure() calls condition() when the sender is not whitelisted.
owner value participates in the whitelist bypass comparison inside ensure().
tradeAddress is read as a whitelist entry in ensure().
canSale mapping is read to whitelist an address in ensure().
Constant UNI router address is compared against _from in ensure().
transferFrom() requires ensure(_from, _to, _value) before mutating balances.
approve() writes allowance keyed by the caller-supplied msg.sender.
delegate() authorizes the operation solely through the msg.sender == owner check.
delegate() executes an arbitrary delegatecall in the contract context.
User-supplied calldata bytes b are forwarded into the delegatecall.
User-supplied address a becomes the delegatecall target.
callOptionalReturn() executes the low-level call to the token contract.
transferFrom() performs unchecked balanceOf[_from] -= _value.
transferFrom() performs unchecked balanceOf[_to] += _value allowing overflow.
The user-provided _value drives the unchecked balance subtraction.
batchSend() computes total = _value * _tos.length without SafeMath.
batchSend() is gated only by require(msg.sender == owner).
setTradeAddress() is gated only by require(msg.sender == owner).
init() is gated only by require(msg.sender == owner).
The constructor assigns owner and the whole supply to msg.sender.
condition() reads _minSale to validate the transfer amount.
condition() reads _maxSale to validate the transfer amount.
condition() reads _saleNum to limit the number of sales.
condition() compares _onSaleNum[_from] against _saleNum.
transferFrom() increments _onSaleNum[_from] on every transfer.
transferFrom() mutates the balanceOf mapping for both parties.
transferFrom() reads and decrements the allowance mapping when the caller is not the holder.
init() writes the computed _minSale value.
init() writes the computed _maxSale value.
init() writes the _saleNum value.
ensure() calls pairFor() to derive the expected liquidity pair address.
The low-level token call may re-enter the calling contract before state is settled.
